summary: Fleet minimal vertical slice plus ProjectCoordinator run-boundary wiring: three mechanical identities (ProjectRecord, ExecutionWorkspace, WorkerLease) with disk-as-single-authority state, CAS reclaim, stale-generation fail-closed fencing and exactly-once settlement; SubAgentRunner acquires the lease at the run boundary (crashed generation superseded on next begin), records fenced facts, settles exactly once at a real terminal, and stays completely fleet-free when no coordinator is injected.

components.disposition: ADMIT. Mechanical ownership facts only: closed-schema state.json, fcntl cross-process lock, atomic replace writes, CAS reclaim, stale-generation fencing, exactly-once settlement. It answers only 'may this physical worker commit side effects/results for this generation'; no task importance, capability ranking, continuation, completion or result-quality judgment is encoded.
evidence: Every write re-reads disk under the lock, so an old coordinator's in-memory handle can never win against a newer generation written by another process.

g1.necessity: SubAgent/worker execution previously had no mechanical answer to 'which physical worker may commit results for the current generation', so a crashed worker's late writes could race a replacement worker — a physical-ownership fact the model cannot verify from outside.

g2.authority_owner: new fleet mechanical identity plane (src/llm_loop/fleet), reusing service_control store conventions (closed schema, fcntl lock, atomic replace)
g2.non_duplication: Does not duplicate service_control deployment binding (services vs execution workspaces), job_registry (local background jobs), or subagent_topology (child sessions); it adds the missing workspace-generation fencing authority only.

g3.recovery_or_reason: Any coordinator can rebuild full state from disk; nothing is held only in memory; revert removes the whole authority with no data migration.

g1.necessity: The store could prove generation ownership, but child execution had no point where that proof was enforced: a run started, mutated, and finished with no mechanical binding between the executing worker and the generation allowed to commit. The run boundary is the only place such a fact can be checked without judging task semantics.

g2.non_duplication: ProjectCoordinator adds no new store, lock, schema or policy; it composes existing store primitives (acquire/reclaim/record_fact/settle/current_lease) behind run-boundary semantics. SubAgentRunner gains one optional constructor dependency; no scheduler, liveness timer, retry policy or capability router is introduced.
